S: My coworker presented the slides I had built all weekend to the director and said he had made them himself.
N: My coworker presented the slides I had built all weekend to the director and said that I had made them.

S: My landlord kept my entire deposit for scuffs that were already listed on the move-in report we both signed.
N: My landlord returned my entire deposit after checking the scuffs that were already listed on the move-in report we both signed.

S: My brother borrowed my car for one evening, returned it three days later with an empty tank, and never mentioned it.
N: My brother borrowed my car for one evening, returned it that night with a full tank, and parked it out front.

S: The airline sold my confirmed seat to someone else and told me at the gate that I would have to wait until tomorrow.
N: The airline moved my confirmed seat to another row and told me at the gate that the flight would board in ten minutes.

S: A friend promised to help me move house, then texted at noon on moving day that he had gone to the beach instead.
N: A friend offered to help me move house, then texted at noon on moving day that he was parking outside the building.

S: My manager rejected my vacation request for the third time and approved the same dates for a colleague who asked later.
N: My manager processed my vacation request on Monday and approved the same dates for a colleague who asked later.

S: The mechanic charged me for replacing brakes, but the old worn pads were still on the car when I checked.
N: The mechanic charged me for replacing brakes, and the new pads were on the car when I checked.

S: My neighbour parked his van across my driveway again, and I missed a job interview because I could not get out.
N: My neighbour parked his van beside my driveway again, and I drove out to a job interview at the usual time.

S: The teacher gave my group project a failing grade because one member copied his section, even though the rest of us wrote ours.
N: The teacher graded my group project section by section, marking each member on the part that he or she had written.

S: A customer service agent promised a callback within an hour; I waited all day and nobody ever phoned back.
N: A customer service agent said a callback would come within an hour; I waited, and the agent phoned back on time.

S: My roommate ate the birthday cake I had bought for my mother and left the empty box in the fridge.
N: My roommate moved the birthday cake I had bought for my mother and left the box on the lower fridge shelf.

S: The referee ignored a clear foul on our striker in the final minute and then gave the other team a penalty for nothing.
N: The referee watched a tackle on our striker in the final minute and then signalled that play should continue normally.

S: Someone online copied my photograph, removed my watermark, and sold prints of it on their own website.
N: Someone online shared my photograph, kept my watermark, and linked to my own website in the caption.

S: The contractor took half the payment upfront, demolished my kitchen, and then stopped answering my calls for six weeks.
N: The contractor took half the payment upfront, demolished my kitchen, and then sent me a schedule for the next six weeks.

S: My sister read my private diary and repeated parts of it to the whole family at Sunday dinner.
N: My sister found my old diary in a box and handed it back to me at Sunday dinner.

S: The clinic cancelled my appointment, which I had waited four months for, by text message two minutes before it began.
N: The clinic confirmed my appointment, which I had waited four months for, by text message two days before it began.

S: My business partner secretly moved our shared savings into his personal account and told me the money was spent on supplies.
N: My business partner moved our shared savings into the supplier account and told me the money was for next month's orders.

S: The city towed my car from a spot where the no-parking sign had been put up only an hour earlier.
N: The city cleaned the street beside my car at a spot where a notice had been put up a week earlier.

S: My boss read my notice email aloud at the team meeting and joked that nobody would notice I was gone.
N: My boss mentioned my notice email at the team meeting and said that my last day would be the end of the month.

S: The hotel gave away our prepaid room and offered us a cot in the conference hall instead.
N: The hotel checked us into our prepaid room and gave us a map of the conference hall.

S: A classmate told the professor I had cheated on the exam, knowing it was false, to improve his own ranking.
N: A classmate told the professor I had finished the exam early, and the professor collected my paper.

S: My uncle sold the old family house without telling anyone, after promising for years that we would decide as a family.
N: My uncle sold the old family house last spring, after the whole family met for years to decide on it as a group.

S: The delivery driver marked my parcel as delivered, but it was never left, and the company refused any refund.
N: The delivery driver marked my parcel as delivered, left it at the front door, and the company emailed a receipt.

S: My teammate skipped every practice all season and was still picked to start the final over me.
N: My teammate attended every practice all season and was picked to start the final beside me.

S: The bank took a forty-dollar fee three times for a single overdraft caused by their own processing delay.
N: The bank showed one forty-dollar fee on my statement for a payment I had made earlier that week.

S: I queued for an hour at the passport office, and the clerk closed the window just as I reached the front.
N: I queued for an hour at the passport office, and the clerk took my form just as I reached the front.

S: My friend posted an unflattering old photo of me online after I had asked her twice to delete it.
N: My friend posted a recent group photo of us online after I had asked her to send me a copy.

S: The landlord entered my flat while I was out, without notice, and went through my desk drawers.
N: The landlord inspected the boiler in my flat while I was home, with a week of notice, as planned.

S: My colleague blamed me in front of the client for a mistake that was entirely in his own report.
N: My colleague explained to the client a correction that had been made in his own report last week.

S: The store refused to honour the warranty on my new laptop, claiming water damage when there was none.
N: The store accepted the warranty claim on my new laptop and sent it to the repair centre that day.

S: My father-in-law corrected my parenting in front of my children at every meal during his two-week visit.
N: My father-in-law talked about his garden at every meal during his two-week visit with my children and me.

S: A driver cut into the queue at the petrol station, took the last pump, and laughed when I pointed it out.
N: A driver pulled into the queue at the petrol station, took the next pump, and nodded when I pointed it out.

S: My landlord raised the rent by forty percent with two weeks of notice, breaking the clause in our lease.
N: My landlord raised the rent by two percent with three months of notice, following the clause in our lease.

S: The insurance company denied my claim after a year of paperwork, citing a rule they added after the accident.
N: The insurance company processed my claim after a year of paperwork, citing the rule that applied at the accident.

S: My friend borrowed five hundred dollars for rent, then spent it on concert tickets and posted pictures from the show.
N: My friend borrowed five hundred dollars for rent, paid it to his landlord, and returned the money the next month.

S: The school principal suspended my son for a fight that video showed another boy had started and finished.
N: The school principal called me about a fight in the yard that video showed involved two other boys.

S: My editor cut my name from an article I had researched for months and put her own byline on it.
N: My editor shortened an article I had researched for months and put my byline on it, as usual.

S: The gym kept charging my card for a year after I cancelled in person and received a written confirmation.
N: The gym stopped charging my card after I cancelled in person and received a written confirmation.

S: My cousin promised to be the best man, then backed out the night before my wedding to go to a party.
N: My cousin agreed to be the best man and arrived the night before my wedding to go over the plans.

S: The recruiter offered me the job, I left my old one, and then they withdrew the offer without a reason.
N: The recruiter offered me the job, I left my old one, and then they sent the contract with a start date.

S: Someone keyed a deep scratch down the side of my new car while it was parked outside my own house.
N: Someone parked a large van down the side of my new car while it was outside my own house.

S: My manager took the bonus that the whole team had earned and spent it on a solo trip for himself.
N: My manager split the bonus that the whole team had earned and paid it into everyone's account on Friday.

S: The tour company cancelled our trip on the morning of departure and kept the full payment as a fee.
N: The tour company moved our trip to a later morning on the day of departure and kept the original price.

S: A neighbour reported me to the council for noise on a night when I was not even home.
N: A neighbour mentioned to the council a night of road works when I was not even home.

S: My group partner submitted our joint essay under his name only and told the tutor I had done nothing.
N: My group partner submitted our joint essay under both our names and told the tutor how we split the work.

S: The restaurant served us an hour late, got every order wrong, and then added a twenty percent service fee.
N: The restaurant served us on time, got every order right, and then added the standard ten percent service fee.

S: My flatmate threw a party in our flat while I was sitting final exams, after promising to keep the flat silent that week.
N: My flatmate held a small party in a friend's flat while I was sitting final exams, as we had arranged for that week.

S: The doctor's receptionist lost my test results twice and then told me it must have been my fault.
N: The doctor's receptionist filed my test results last week and then told me the doctor would review them.

S: My employer cut my hours in half the week after I raised a safety issue with the regional office.
N: My employer kept my hours the same the week after I raised a safety issue with the regional office.

S: A stranger took the parking space I had been waiting for with my indicator on and walked off smiling.
N: A stranger left the parking space I had been waiting for with my indicator on, and I pulled into it.

S: My mother gave away my childhood books to a charity shop after I had asked her to store them for me.
N: My mother packed my childhood books into boxes and kept them in the attic after I had asked her to store them.

S: The train company sold more tickets than seats, and I stood for four hours on a reserved journey.
N: The train company sold tickets for every seat, and I sat for four hours on a reserved journey.

S: The council promised to fix the broken streetlight on our road and has ignored every report for two years.
N: The council said it would fix the broken streetlight on our road and replaced it two weeks later.

S: My co-founder signed a major deal on behalf of our company without consulting me, against our written agreement.
N: My co-founder signed a major deal on behalf of our company after consulting me, as our written agreement requires.

S: The phone company switched me to a more expensive plan without asking and refused to switch me back.
N: The phone company switched me to a new plan at the same price after asking and sent the details by email.

S: A colleague kept interrupting me in every meeting and then repeated my ideas as his own a minute later.
N: A colleague spoke after me in every meeting and then added his own points to my ideas a minute later.

S: My neighbour cut down the tree on my side of the fence while I was away, without asking.
N: My neighbour trimmed the hedge on his side of the fence while I was away, as he does each year.

S: The university lost my thesis file and then charged me a late fee for sending it again.
N: The university received my thesis file and then emailed me a receipt with the reference number.

S: My friend told everyone at work about my health problem after I asked her to keep it private.
N: My friend asked me at lunch about my health appointment, which I had mentioned to her the week before.

S: The car rental company billed me for damage that was clearly marked on the form when I collected the car.
N: The car rental company checked the damage that was clearly marked on the form when I collected the car.

S: My boss scheduled a mandatory meeting on my day off and then wrote me up for being absent.
N: My boss scheduled a team meeting on my day off and then sent me the notes the next morning.

S: The coach benched my daughter for the whole tournament because she had missed one practice for a funeral.
N: The coach rotated my daughter in for half of the tournament, as he did with every player on the team.

S: A seller online took my payment for concert tickets and then blocked me without sending anything.
N: A seller online took my payment for concert tickets and then sent the tickets to my email that evening.

S: My aunt told the whole family that I had stolen money from my grandmother, which was completely untrue.
N: My aunt told the whole family that I had collected money for my grandmother, which was accurate.

S: The building manager shut off our water for three days with no warning during a heat wave.
N: The building manager shut off our water for three hours, as announced a week earlier, during repairs.

S: My housemate used my toothbrush to clean the bathroom tiles and put it back in my cup.
N: My housemate used an old brush to clean the bathroom tiles and put it back under the sink.

S: The tax office fined me for late filing, although their own website had crashed on the deadline day.
N: The tax office processed my filing, which I had sent through their website on the deadline day.

S: My manager promised me a promotion if I covered his projects for a year, then gave it to his nephew.
N: My manager asked me to cover his projects for a year, then reviewed my work at the end of it.

S: A cyclist rode through the red signal, hit my side mirror, and rode away while shouting insults at me.
N: A cyclist stopped at the red signal beside my side mirror, and rode away when the signal changed.

S: My best friend started dating my partner while I was abroad and kept it from me for months.
N: My best friend started a new job while I was abroad and told me about it in a letter.

S: The plumber left without finishing, flooded the bathroom, and then demanded double payment for an emergency visit.
N: The plumber finished the job, tested the bathroom pipes, and then asked for the payment we had agreed on.

S: My co-worker reported my late arrival to HR on the one day I was nursing my sick child.
N: My co-worker noted my late arrival in the shared calendar on the one day I had a dentist appointment.

S: The internet provider promised installation on Monday, missed four appointments, and still charged me for the month.
N: The internet provider arranged installation on Monday, arrived on time, and charged me for the month.

S: My teenage son lied about going to the library and took the car out with friends overnight.
N: My teenage son said he was going to the library and took the bus there with friends after school.

S: The team captain changed the match time without telling me, so I was dropped for not showing up.
N: The team captain changed the match time and told me in advance, so I arrived for the new start.

S: A colleague ate my labelled lunch from the shared office fridge for the third day in a row.
N: A colleague moved my labelled lunch to the top shelf of the office fridge for the third day in a row.

S: The airline lost my suitcase, refused to compensate me, and closed my claim without reading it.
N: The airline delayed my suitcase, delivered it to my hotel, and closed my claim after reading it.

S: My sister-in-law changed the holiday plans that I had paid for and booked her own family into my room.
N: My sister-in-law checked the holiday plans that I had paid for and booked her own family into the next room.

S: The software company deleted my account and all my files without warning after a billing error on their side.
N: The software company moved my account and all my files to a new server after a billing update on their side.

S: My professor promised me a reference letter, then missed the deadline and never replied to my reminders.
N: My professor agreed to write a reference letter, sent it before the deadline, and replied to my reminder.

S: A man in the cinema talked on his phone through the whole film and told me to mind my own business.
N: A man in the cinema switched off his phone before the film and asked me what time it would end.

S: The council approved a building that blocks all sunlight to our garden, after promising residents a public hearing.
N: The council approved a building at the end of our street, after holding a public hearing with residents.

S: My partner spent our wedding savings on a motorbike without telling me and said it was his money too.
N: My partner moved our wedding savings into a fixed account after telling me and said it paid more interest.

S: The supermarket charged me twice for the same shopping and the manager refused to check the receipt.
N: The supermarket charged me once for the shopping and the manager handed me a printed receipt.

S: A client refused to pay my invoice after using all my designs, claiming the work had never been ordered.
N: A client paid my invoice after using all my designs, noting the work had been ordered in March.

S: My neighbour's dog dug up my vegetable garden again, and he said I should build a better fence.
N: My neighbour's dog walked past my vegetable garden again, and he said he was taking it to the park.

S: My boss read my private messages on the work computer and quoted them back to me during my review.
N: My boss checked the shared files on the work computer and discussed them with me during my review.

S: The ticket inspector fined me for having no ticket, though I showed him the valid one on my phone.
N: The ticket inspector checked my ticket, and I showed him the valid one on my phone.

S: My grandfather left his savings to the cousin who never visited, after the rest of us nursed him for years.
N: My grandfather divided his savings equally among all the grandchildren, who had each visited him regularly over the years.

S: A colleague went on a two-week holiday the week of our deadline and left his half of the work undone.
N: A colleague took a two-week holiday the week after our deadline and finished his half of the work first.

S: The removal company broke my piano during the move and then denied ever having carried it.
N: The removal company carried my piano during the move and then placed it where I had asked.

S: My friend invited everyone from our group to her birthday party except me and posted the photos online.
N: My friend invited everyone from our group to her birthday party, including me, and posted the photos online.

S: The hospital billed me for a scan that was never done and sent the bill to a debt collector.
N: The hospital billed me for the scan that was done last month and sent the bill to my home address.

S: My landlord refused to repair the broken heating all winter but still raised the rent in January.
N: My landlord repaired the broken heating in early winter and kept the rent the same in January.

S: A shop assistant followed me around the store and searched my bag, while ignoring the other customers.
N: A shop assistant walked past me in the store and stocked a shelf, while the other customers browsed.

S: My partner forgot to pick our daughter up from school again, leaving her waiting alone for two hours.
N: My partner picked our daughter up from school again, and they arrived home at the usual time.

S: The election office removed my name from the voter list by mistake and refused to let me vote.
N: The election office found my name on the voter list and handed me a ballot paper to vote.

S: My colleague told our manager that I had agreed to work every weekend this month, which I never did.
N: My colleague told our manager that I would work one weekend this month, which we had arranged.

S: The bus driver saw me running toward the stop, looked straight at me, and pulled away early.
N: The bus driver saw me walking toward the stop, waited at the kerb, and pulled away on schedule.

S: My brother-in-law borrowed my tools for a weekend and sold them at a market a month later.
N: My brother-in-law borrowed my tools for a weekend and returned them in a box the following Monday.

S: The phone shop sold me a used phone as new, and the manager said all sales were final.
N: The phone shop sold me a new phone, and the manager explained the return policy at the till.

S: A classmate erased my files from the shared drive the night before our presentation and denied it.
N: A classmate backed up my files on the shared drive the night before our presentation and told me.

S: My neighbour piled his rubbish bags against my front door every week for a month.
N: My neighbour put his rubbish bags beside the communal bin every week for a month.

S: The company announced my project at a conference and gave all the credit to a director who had never worked on it.
N: The company announced my project at a conference and named me and the two engineers who had worked on it.

S: My friend cancelled our dinner plans for the fifth time, an hour after I had arrived at the restaurant.
N: My friend moved our dinner plans to the next night, a week before we were due at the restaurant.

S: The repair service kept my washing machine for two months and returned it still broken, with a large bill.
N: The repair service kept my washing machine for two days and returned it working, with the quoted bill.

S: A passenger put his bag on the only free seat on the train and refused to move it for an elderly woman.
N: A passenger put his bag on the rack above the train seats and offered the free seat to an elderly woman.

S: My manager announced in the team chat that my mistake had cost the company money, though it was his decision.
N: My manager announced in the team chat that his decision had changed the budget, and listed the new figures.

S: The council fined me for putting my bins out on the wrong day, after changing the schedule without notice.
N: The council emailed me about putting my bins out on a new day, after changing the schedule with notice.

S: My father promised to come to my graduation, then booked a golf weekend for the same date.
N: My father said he would come to my graduation, then booked a train for the same date.

S: A coworker kept taking extended breaks and logging my sales under her name to reach her monthly target.
N: A coworker kept taking short breaks and logging her own sales under her name to reach her monthly target.

S: The estate agent showed my flat to buyers while I was in the shower, after letting himself in.
N: The estate agent showed my flat to buyers while I was at work, after arranging it with me by phone.

S: My friend promised to feed my cat while I was away and forgot completely for four days.
N: My friend agreed to feed my cat while I was away and stopped by twice a day for four days.

S: The online store sent me a broken television and then refused a return, saying I must have dropped it.
N: The online store sent me a new television and then emailed a return label, as with every order.

S: A tutor gave my essay a low mark for being too short, though it was exactly the required length.
N: A tutor gave my essay a mark for its length, which was exactly the required length.

S: My neighbours held a loud party until four in the morning on a weeknight and ignored my knocking.
N: My neighbours held a small party until ten in the evening on a weekend and opened the door when I knocked.

S: My boss promised to sign off my training course, then said there was no budget and sent his favourite instead.
N: My boss reviewed my training course request, then checked the budget and sent me the booking details that afternoon.

S: The airline charged me fifty dollars for a bag that met every size rule on their own website.
N: The airline weighed my bag, which met every size rule on their own website, and printed a tag.

S: My son's school sent him home without lunch because of a payment error made by their own office.
N: My son's school sent home a note about lunch because of a payment update made by their own office.

S: A colleague shared my unfinished draft with the whole department and wrote that it showed my lack of effort.
N: A colleague shared my finished draft with the whole department and wrote that comments were due on Friday.

S: The building owner promised a working lift, but it has been broken for a year and I carry groceries up eight floors.
N: The building owner said the lift would be serviced, and it was repaired within a day, so I took groceries up eight floors.

S: A driver behind me honked at a red signal for a full minute and then tailgated me for miles.
N: A driver behind me waited at a red signal for a full minute and then followed the traffic for miles.

S: My stepmother changed the locks on my father's house and refused to let me collect my belongings.
N: My stepmother changed the locks on my father's house and gave me a new key to collect my belongings.

S: The streaming service doubled its price overnight and removed the shows I was paying for.
N: The streaming service kept its price the same overnight and added a new section to the menu.

S: My doctor dismissed my symptoms for a year, and another doctor found the problem in one visit.
N: My doctor reviewed my symptoms over a year, and another doctor ran the same test in one visit.

S: A teammate posted a screenshot of my missed goal online with a caption mocking my skills.
N: A teammate posted a screenshot of our match online with a caption listing the final result.

S: The landlord gave my reserved parking spot to a new tenant while I was still paying for it.
N: The landlord gave a new tenant the parking spot next to mine while I was still paying for mine.

S: My manager changed the deadline to tomorrow at five in the evening, after I had planned my week around Friday.
N: My manager confirmed the deadline for Friday at five in the evening, after I had planned my week around it.

S: My cousin borrowed my wedding dress for her own wedding and returned it stained and torn.
N: My cousin borrowed my wedding dress for her own wedding and returned it cleaned and in its bag.

S: The bank froze my account for a week by mistake, and my rent payment bounced as a result.
N: The bank updated my account over a weekend, and my rent payment went through on Monday as a result.

S: A colleague spread a rumour that I was being fired, and two clients moved their accounts away.
N: A colleague mentioned that I was being transferred, and two clients moved their accounts to my new office.

S: My flatmate moved out without notice and left me to pay his share of the rent for three months.
N: My flatmate moved out with notice and paid his share of the rent until a new tenant arrived.

S: The ferry left twenty minutes early with my booked car space empty, and the company refused a refund.
N: The ferry left on time with my booked car space filled, and the company emailed me a receipt.

S: My old friend asked to borrow my thesis notes, then published them in a paper with only his name.
N: My old friend asked to borrow my thesis notes, then returned them with a list of the papers he had read.

S: The waiter brought everyone at my table their food but forgot my order three times.
N: The waiter brought everyone at my table their food, and my order came out with the rest.

S: My neighbour planted a fence a metre into my garden and told the surveyor I had agreed to it.
N: My neighbour planted a fence along the old line of my garden and told the surveyor I had seen the plans.

S: My company announced layoffs by email on Christmas Eve, the day after paying executives large bonuses.
N: My company announced the new office hours by email on Christmas Eve, the day after the board meeting.

S: A man at the post office pushed ahead of the whole queue and the clerk served him first.
N: A man at the post office joined the end of the queue and the clerk served him in turn.

S: My brother told our parents that I had crashed their car, when he had been driving it himself.
N: My brother told our parents that he had parked their car, when he had been driving it himself.

S: The landlord said my rent check had never arrived, but he had already cashed it the week before.
N: The landlord said my rent check had arrived, and he had cashed it the week before.

S: A fellow student took the library book I had reserved, then lent it to his friend for the whole term.
N: A fellow student returned the library book I had reserved, and the desk held it for me for the term.

S: My boss made me redo a report from scratch, then submitted the original version with his name on it.
N: My boss asked me to update a report from scratch, then submitted the new version with my name on it.

S: The phone company cut off my service while I was abroad, although I had paid every bill on time.
N: The phone company sent me a roaming message while I was abroad, as I had paid every bill on time.

S: My mother-in-law threw away my homemade dinner and served takeaway, saying my cooking was not good enough.
N: My mother-in-law put away my homemade dinner and served it the next day with some bread from the shop.

S: The umpire changed the line call after the opposing coach shouted at him, and we lost the set.
N: The umpire checked the line call after the opposing coach asked him, and the point was replayed.

S: A moderator deleted my forum post and banned me, while leaving the identical post by his friend.
N: A moderator moved my forum post to another thread, along with the identical post by his friend.

S: My employer paid me two weeks late for the third month running and blamed me for asking.
N: My employer paid me on the usual date for the third month running and sent a payslip by email.

S: My friend booked the last two seats for the show I had told him about and went with someone else.
N: My friend booked two seats for the show I had told him about and sent me the ticket number.

S: The gas company sent a bill four times larger than usual and refused to read the meter again.
N: The gas company sent a bill the same size as usual and arranged to read the meter again in spring.

S: A colleague signed my name on a petition against our manager without asking me first.
N: A colleague showed me a petition about our office hours and asked me if I would read it.

S: My younger sister broke the camera I had saved a year for and hid it in my closet.
N: My younger sister used the camera I had saved a year for and put it back in my closet.

S: The hotel posted my passport details on a public notice board in the lobby by mistake.
N: The hotel copied my passport details at the front desk in the lobby during check-in.

S: A director promised our team a slower month, then accepted three new urgent projects for us the next day.
N: A director told our team the plan for the month, then listed three new projects for us the next day.

S: The visa office rejected my application for a missing document that I had included and they had stamped.
N: The visa office processed my application with the document that I had included and they had stamped.

S: My neighbour let his children throw stones at my windows and said they were just playing.
N: My neighbour let his children draw with chalk on the pavement and said they were just playing.

S: A friend asked me to cover for her at work and then told our boss I had insisted on swapping shifts.
N: A friend asked me to cover for her at work and then told our boss that we had swapped shifts.

S: The seller listed the flat as having a garden, but after we signed it turned out to be a shared car park.
N: The seller listed the flat as having a garden, and after we signed it turned out to be a small lawn.

S: My manager gave my desk by the window to an intern while I was on parental leave.
N: My manager gave an intern the desk next to mine by the window while I was on parental leave.

S: The pharmacy gave me the wrong medicine twice in a month and blamed my doctor's handwriting.
N: The pharmacy gave me my medicine twice in a month and printed my doctor's instructions on the label.

S: My friend used my credit card details to order things online, saying he would have paid me back eventually.
N: My friend used his own credit card details to order things online, saying the parcel would come on Tuesday.

S: The organiser removed my stall from the market after I had paid the fee, to make room for a sponsor.
N: The organiser moved my stall in the market after I had paid the fee, to make room for a walkway.

S: My son's coach shouted at the children after every missed pass and sent my son home in the rain.
N: My son's coach spoke to the children after every training session and drove my son home in the rain.

S: A colleague reserved the only meeting room for a whole week, then never used it while my client waited outside.
N: A colleague reserved the meeting room for a whole week, then used it while my client met me in the next room.

S: My neighbour's builders started drilling at six every morning, against the agreed hours, for three weeks.
N: My neighbour's builders started drilling at nine every morning, within the agreed hours, for three weeks.

S: The courier left my new laptop on the street outside the wrong house and marked it signed by me.
N: The courier left my new laptop with the neighbour I had named and marked it signed by her.

S: My brother skipped our mother's surgery day to watch a football match after promising to drive her.
N: My brother drove our mother to the hospital on her surgery day and then watched a football match.

S: A landlord advertised the flat as allowing cats, then fined us for our cat a month after we moved in.
N: A landlord advertised the flat as allowing cats, then added our cat to the lease a month after we moved in.

S: My teammate sold our shared research idea to a startup and never told anyone in our lab.
N: My teammate presented our shared research idea to a startup and told everyone in our lab.

S: The library charged me for a book I had returned, and the staff refused to look at the return slip I kept.
N: The library emailed me about a book I had returned, and the staff looked at the return slip I kept.

S: The dentist's office double-booked my slot, sent me home after an hour, and still billed me for a missed appointment.
N: The dentist's office moved my slot, called me an hour ahead, and billed me for the new appointment.
